Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). The guess of why: Cubic is stuck in exponential RTO backoff after initial loss, so queue-length changes alone are unlikely to make Cubic deliver data.

  [Y4] guess: TCP sent an initial window and reduced cwnd/ssthresh after loss; the forward FIFO is full at about 100 packets, so TCP packets are dropped before ACKs rather than the receiver advertising a zero window.

THE RESULT the guess is about: r006 scheduler Cubic q1000 has tcp_inflight mean/max 1,048,576 bytes, tcp_rtt_ms mean 17.217 ms, and tcp_goodput_bps 476,482,765; r007 scheduler BBR q1000 has tcp_inflight max 8,688 bytes, tcp_rtt_ms mean 0.220 ms, and tcp_goodput_bps 190,096,915.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: Cubic's scheduler goodput comes from holding a about 1 MiB inflight over a scheduler-induced 17 ms RTT, near its scheduler share; BBR keeps only about BDP inflight and underfills, so queue length must be large enough to hold Cubic's inflight.
THE HYPOTHESIS H14: With sender-side scheduler and TcpCubic, tcp_goodput_bps at l1.queue.length=1000 exceeds tcp_goodput_bps at l1.queue.length=4 by more than 10 Mbps, and tcp_inflight_max at q4 is below 10% of tcp_inflight_max at q1000.
DECISION RULE: (tcp_goodput_bps@sched_cubic_q1000 - tcp_goodput_bps@sched_cubic_q4) > max(10000000, 0.01 * max(tcp_goodput_bps@sched_cubic_q1000, tcp_goodput_bps@sched_cubic_q4)) AND tcp_inflight_max@sched_cubic_q4 < 0.1 * tcp_inflight_max@sched_cubic_q1000
A MEASUREMENT THE RESEARCHER DEFINES FOR THIS TEST: tcp_inflight_max = max of tcp_inflight, from 2 s to the end (computed by the harness from what each simulation records; the probe only listens)
Between the simulations its rule compares, the one setting that differs: l1.queue.length; the measure the rule is about: tcp_goodput_bps
THE SIMULATIONS PLANNED FOR IT:
  sched_cubic_q1000 {l1.queue.length=1000, tcp.type=TcpCubic}  (already run as S6: its result is in the table above and will be returned, not run again)
  sched_cubic_q4 {l1.queue.length=4, tcp.type=TcpCubic}  (new)

Before any of these simulations is run: can this test tell whether the guess is true? First name the strongest rival explanation you can think of and say what the decision rule would do under it. Then say what would make you doubt the test even if it comes out as predicted. Then name the defect, or none. The defects: none: no defect; not_about_the_guess: the hypothesis would come out the same whether the guess is true or not, or is about another cause than the guess; rival_passes_too: a rival explanation predicts the same outcome of the decision rule, so the test cannot tell the two apart; already_answered: records already in the ledger give the result this test asks for: read it from them instead of simulating again; confounded: another setting, at the values chosen, limits or hides the effect, so the result would not show what the hypothesis says; threshold: the rule's threshold or margin makes it hold or fail whatever happens, or lies inside the tolerance. A test is not defective for being small or for testing only one consequence of the guess.

answer.rival: A strong rival is that q4 simply caps or drops TCP because the 4-packet queue is too small, so any TCP would show lower inflight and goodput; under this rival the rule would still pass if q4 goodput falls by more than 10 Mbps and q4 inflight stays below 104,857.6 bytes, which is 10% of r006's 1,048,576-byte inflight.
answer.doubt_if: I would doubt it if q4's low inflight is just the queue cap or loss, or if q4's RTT is not the 17.217 ms seen in r006, because then the result would show generic starvation rather than Cubic holding 1 MiB over a scheduler-induced RTT.
answer.because: r006 already shows tcp_inflight max 1,048,576 bytes equal to tcp_rwnd max 1,048,576 bytes, so the 1 MiB inflight may be receiver-window limited rather than Cubic-specific.

The result it starts from, as the researcher states it: r005 FIFO LinuxReno q1000 has tcp_goodput_bps=5792 and tcp_cwnd_max=107152, while r006 scheduler Cubic q1000 has tcp_goodput_bps=476482765.
The guess of why: Under a scheduler, LinuxReno's growth is enough to fill the same per-flow share as Cubic.

THE SESSION'S EARLIER GUESSES AND HYPOTHESES:
  [Y1] guess: The FIFO queue is full from UDP excess, so TCP packets are tail-dropped before TCP can establish or deliver data.
  [Y2] guess: TCP is retransmitting lost connection or data segments after a long RTO rather than making progress.
  [Y3] guess: TCP's initial window is lost immediately and the flow is not making progress; the later cwnd value likely reflects a new connection attempt or reset rather than successful congestion control.
  [Y4] guess: TCP sent an initial window and reduced cwnd/ssthresh after loss; the forward FIFO is full at about 100 packets, so TCP packets are dropped before ACKs rather than the receiver advertising a zero window.
  [Y5] guess: Loss-based Cubic backs off under this high loss, whereas BBR's bandwidth/delay estimation may keep inflight and deliver more.
  [Y6] guess: Cubic's zero goodput is not a zero-window or no-connection stall; it sends an initial window, loses it in the full FIFO, and exponential RTO backoff keeps it near zero.
  [Y7] guess: For BBR, queue 4 is below its BDP and will drop its own inflight, whereas queue 100 can hold BBR's inflight and should give higher goodput.
  [Y8] guess: Cubic is stuck in exponential RTO backoff after initial loss, so queue-length changes alone are unlikely to make Cubic deliver data.
  [Y9] guess: For BBR, a larger FIFO lets more TCP packets survive and be buffered behind UDP, so queue 1000 should give more goodput than queue 100.
  [Y10] guess: Queue 1000 may be large enough for Cubic's initial window and ACKs to survive, so Cubic may deliver data; BBR may deliver less because it keeps inflight near BDP.
  [Y11] guess: The sender-side FIFO under UDP saturation gives TCP almost no service; queue length only buffers UDP and increases delay, so TCP type cannot recover.
  [Y12] guess: Replacing the sender-side FIFO with a scheduler will allocate a link share to TCP and raise tcp_goodput_bps substantially.

THE NEW GUESS
The result it starts from, as the researcher states it: r009 scheduler Cubic q100 has tcp_goodput_bps=482007923, tcp_inflight_max=159280, and tcp_rtt_mean=2.093 ms, while r006 scheduler Cubic q1000 has tcp_goodput_bps=476482765, tcp_inflight_max=1048576, and tcp_rtt_mean=17.217 ms.
The guess of why: The scheduler share caps TCP; q100 is near that share, q4 may be too small to hold enough inflight, and LinuxReno at q100 should fill the same share because the 1 MiB receive window is not limiting there.

  [Y2] guess: TCP is retransmitting lost connection or data segments after a long RTO rather than making progress.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.
